title: Interesting Facts About Number 37 - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Many people tend to pick the number 37 when asked to choose a random number between 1 and 100. This is part of the "Randomness Paradox," which shows that our idea of randomness isn't as random as we think. Psychologists found a similar pattern called the "Blue-Seven Phenomenon," where people often choose blue and 7 when asked to pick a random color and number. In surveys, 7 is the most common single-digit number, and for two-digit numbers, 37 is the most popular.

Some Interesting Facts about Number 37

  • 37 is the fifth Lucky prime number (e.g., 3, 7, 13, 19, 37, 43, 67, 73, 79, 97...)
  • 37 is fourth centered hexagonal number (e.g., 1, 7, 19, 37, 61...)
  • 37 is the third star number (e.g. 1, 13, 37, 73, 121, 253, 337, 433, ...)
  • 37 is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 9 = 37; also 12345679 × 3 = 37037037
  • Multiplying 37 by numbers like 3, 33, 333, or 3333 will produce palindromic results. For example: 37 × 3 = 111, 37 × 33 = 1221, 37 × 333 = 12321, 37 × 3333 = 123321...
  • If a three-digit number is divisible by 37, its cyclic permutations are also divisible by 37. For example: if XYZ = 148 (a multiple of 37), then both YZX = 481 and ZXY = 814 are also multiples of 37.
  • The smallest magic square that uses only prime numbers and 1 has 37 in the middle cell.
    \begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline 31 & 73 & 7 \\ \hline 13 & \mathbf{37} & 61 \\ \hline 67 & 1 & 43 \\ \hline \end{array}

Mathematical Importance of Number 37

The number 37 is not just a simple prime; it holds a significant place in maths due to its unique properties and classifications. As a prime number, it can't be divided by any other numbers besides 1 and itself.

Number 37 is Classified as :

1. Emirp: The reverse of 37 is 73, which is also prime, so 37 is an emirp.

2. Lucky Prime : 37 is part of the sequence of lucky numbers, and it is 5th lucky prime.

3. Sexy Prime: 37 is a sexy prime because it is 6 more than 31 and 6 less than 43.

4. Permutable Prime: Its digits can be rearranged to form another prime i.e., 73.

5. Padovan Prime: It is 15th term of the Padovan sequence and fifth prime in this sequence.

6. Strong Prime: A prime that is greater than the arithmetic mean of the nearest primes on either side (31 and 41).

7. Pythagorean Prime: A prime of the form 4n + 1 (for 37, n = 9)

8. Star Number : 37 is the third star number.

9. Cuban Prime: It can be expressed in the form ( \frac{4^3 – 3^3}{4 – 3} = \frac{64 – 27}{1} = 37 ).

Magic of Number 37

The fascinating patterns hidden in the number 37 are:

Sum of Digits

Take a single digit number, for such as 9:

Write it 3 times, to form : 999

Add the digits: (9 + 9 + 9) = 27

Now divide the number with its digit sum, and you will get: 999 ÷ 27 = 37

Palindromic Multiplication Pattern

Multiplying 37 by numbers consisting entirely of the digit 3 creates symmetrical results.

Examples:

37 × 3 = 111

37 × 33 = 1221

37 × 333 = 12321

37 × 3333 = 123321

These products form attractive numerical patterns that make 37 a favorite among recreational mathematicians.
